why: Item 1 holds: check 3 lists every exported function and fails if any one is missing, so a README that documents clamp but not subtract fails. Item 2 is broken by the same check. Its command passes a function only if README.md contains the literal text `name(`, as in `!md.includes(n+"(")`. Line 3 only asks that every exported function be documented. A README that says "`subtract` — returns a minus b" documents subtract but would fail. Requiring signature-style text is a specific README layout, which is stricter than the line. Check 4 is also somewhat strict: it requires the TAP summary to show '# fail 0', but Node's test runner can print a different summary format depending on the output. Checks 1 and 2 match their lines: they test the values clamp returns and that it throws a RangeError for any message.
